dedupe_keys.name: national long distance passenger travel demand model rjourney

description: The National Long-Distance Passenger Travel Demand Model is a prototype national model of trips over 100 miles in the United States, built under the Federal Highway Administration's Exploratory Advanced Research programme to analyse regionally and nationally significant passenger corridors alongside freight and local travel. It is multimodal, covering car, bus, rail and air, and estimates long-distance travel patterns and demand for policy and corridor scenarios. FHWA released all project products for reuse by agencies and businesses in statewide and regional modelling: reports on the fundamentals and development, a user guide, the rJourney demand model software (version 1.3.2, zip download), assignment procedures for TransCAD and the National User Model Area zone system as shapefiles, free to download from the FHWA page, which was last modified in October 2018; the page states no licence. Caveats: it is a research prototype that FHWA says it will test further, highway assignment needs the commercial TransCAD package, and the BTS resilience hub notes that using it requires technical expertise in travel modelling software. It supports national capacity planning and network flow scenarios for long-distance corridors, and can be combined with the NHTS for calibration.
